item.title: Research
item.description: I am currently supported with funding as an NSF Graduate Research Fellow. In general, I am interested in PDE and their applications to physics. I don’t have an “official” advisor at the moment, but I have been working on some research problems with Dr. Isaac Harric the past few semesters. Recently I have been working on proving the well posedness of the Biharmonic scattering problem for small domains, and hope to have a paper drafted at some point in the future.

item.title: Teaching
item.description: Though am am supported through the NSF GRFP, I still serve as a teaching assistant in the math department. For students, any appropriate files (if applicable) will be linked by clicking on the semester you took it. item.title: About
item.description: I am originally from Topeka, KS and I completed my undergrad in Mathematics and Physics at Kansas State University. I came to Purdue because their Math department is one of the few in the country that actually has a research group for Scattering Theory. After my PhD, my goal is to stay in academia and teach and conduct research full time. Given the current climate and job market I am flexible in that goal however…

item.title: A Beginner's Guide to the Sun \& Moon through Lost Thunder Format
item.description: Table of Contents 1: An Introduction to SUM-LOT 2: Important Cards Supporters Items Stadiums Pokemon 3: An Overview of the Metagame 4: Decklists An Introduction to SUM-LOT The Sun and Moon era of the Pokemon TCG is looked back on extremely fondly by competitively players, and rightly so. After the dominance of big-basic strategies in the Black and White era, and them continuing into XY due to the lackluster Mega Evolution mechanic, it was exciting to see the evolving Pokemon GX take over the reigns.
